Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: ONE standalone square transparent ore mineral overlay, authored on a LOGICAL 16x16 Minecraft pixel grid for exact center-point reduction.
Primary request: Ironstone, variant 1, FRAGMENT role. One small transparent notch breaks the exposure. Deposit identity: oolitic sedimentary ironstone lens. Style/medium: bold deliberate Minecraft Java 16x16 pixel art. Every visible shape is built from large hard-edged square logical pixels, each logical pixel approximately one-sixteenth of the canvas width. Use coarse contiguous clusters, not finely painted high-resolution detail. Crisp stepped boundaries and mostly opaque mineral cells.
Composition/framing: One short incomplete stepped trace/lens about 2 logical pixels thick and 5–7 logical pixels long, approximately 14–28 visible cells after exact sampling. One natural edge contact if it fits. One physically connected formation, with only a small clear notch if needed. Most of the face clear. Do not use hairlines, subpixel scratches, tiny isolated grains, antialiased miniature painting, full-face seam/network, or centered nugget.
Materials/textures: earthy medium gray-brown, quiet ochre/rust interior patches, darker oolitic grouping; no saturated orange. Group two close physical medium values INSIDE the formation; enough contrast to read against mid-gray stone, but no pale outline, dark border, highlight rail, or carved/raised relief. No blanket alpha fade.
Constraints: exactly one 1:1 square PNG at least 1024x1024, untouched mineral overlay with genuine alpha and hard pixel clusters; no stone/deepslate pixels, text, labels, watermark, frame.
Avoid: round rust blob, coin, metallic bar, orange outline; isolated one-pixel speck, blurry fringe, decorative confetti, whole-block emblem, smooth gradients, glow, shadow, haze, high-resolution realism.
disposition: Retained unchanged as first pattern within category; active human review
